Description: Hamburger toggle (desktop collapse + mobile overlay drawer), plus a per-section accordion for each nav heading
Acceptance Criteria: Clicking the hamburger collapses/expands the whole sidebar (desktop: reflow; mobile: overlay drawer with backdrop); clicking a section heading (OVERVIEW/AUDIENCE/SETTINGS) independently expands/collapses just that section's items
Required Tests: Frontend component tests
Evidence: Direct user request (ad hoc, not from a prior sprint plan), asked mid-session after `GRX-AUDIT-002`, in two parts. **Part 1 — whole-sidebar hamburger toggle.** Introduced this app's first responsive breakpoint (768px) — none existed before. New `DashboardShell` client component (extracted from `layout.tsx`, which stays a server component doing the auth check) owns a single `sidebarOpen` boolean and renders the hamburger button (inline SVG, no icon library in this project); `Sidebar` gained `open`/`onClose` props and a conditionally-rendered backdrop `<button>`. One boolean drives both breakpoints via CSS alone: at desktop widths `open=false` collapses width to 0 (flex reflow, no per-item icons exist so this is a full hide, not an icon-only rail); at mobile widths (`@media (max-width: 768px)`) the sidebar is `position: fixed` and translates off-screen by default, with `.mobileOpen` sliding it to `translateX(0)` — no JS media-query branching needed for the toggle itself. A `useEffect` keyed on `usePathname()` closes the drawer on navigation whenever `window.matchMedia("(max-width: 768px)")` matches, so navigating on mobile doesn't leave the drawer covering the new page; desktop navigation is unaffected since nothing calls `onClose` on link click there. Added a `window.matchMedia` polyfill to `vitest.setup.ts` (jsdom has none) — a real gap this exposed, now available to any future test needing it. **Part 2 — per-section accordion**, requested immediately after as a follow-up referencing a third-party product screenshot (per-heading expand/collapse, e.g. "Market"/"Automation"): each `NAV_SECTIONS` entry (OVERVIEW/AUDIENCE/SETTINGS) is now its own independent accordion via a `Record<string, boolean>` keyed by section label, defaulting every section to expanded (non-breaking — matches prior always-visible behavior); the plain `<span>` section label became a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and a rotating chevron SVG. Complementary to, not a replacement for, the whole-sidebar toggle — collapsing one section doesn't affect the others or the sidebar's own open/closed state. `eslint`/`tsc --noEmit`/`prettier --check` clean; `vitest` 54 passed (4 new: default-open desktop + toggle, default-closed mobile via a `matchMedia` spy, permission-based nav filtering still holds through the prop changes, and independent per-section collapse/expand); `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright, 4 tests, unaffected by either change) still passes against a real `next build`. Live-verified against the rebuilt `web` container at both `desktop` and `mobile` (375×812) presets: desktop hamburger click smoothly collapses/expands the sidebar with content reflow; mobile loads with the sidebar off-screen by default (no flash-then-hide), hamburger opens it as a dimmed overlay drawer, clicking a nav link navigates and auto-closes the drawer, clicking the backdrop also closes it; clicking the "AUDIENCE" heading collapsed its 5 items (chevron rotated) while "OVERVIEW"/"SETTINGS" stayed expanded and unaffected, re-clicking restored it. Task: Scheduler ticker, worker dispatch consumer, idempotency/retry, DLQ, tests
Description: Poll `campaigns` for due `SCHEDULED` rows and dispatch them via a RabbitMQ worker with Redis idempotency and exponential-backoff retry
Acceptance Criteria: A `SCHEDULED` campaign past its `scheduled_at` is atomically claimed, dispatched by the worker, retried up to 3x with 1m/5m/15m backoff on transient failure, and lands in `grx.campaigns.dlq` + `FAILED` after exhausting retries
Required Tests: `test_campaign_scheduler_ticker.py` (3), `test_dispatch_consumer.py` (4), full `pytest`/`ruff`/`mypy`/`alembic check` both apps
Evidence: Per the user's explicit instruction to build the rest of Sprint 4 rather than just document the gap. **Scheduler (`GRX-SCHED-002`)**: `claim_due_campaigns()` does a single `UPDATE campaigns SET status='DISPATCHING' WHERE status='SCHEDULED' AND scheduled_at <= NOW() RETURNING *` (safe under concurrent tickers via Postgres row locks, unlike SELECT-then-UPDATE), then `run_scheduler_tick()` commits and publishes one `grx.campaigns.dispatch` job per claimed campaign; `run_scheduler_loop()` runs forever as a `FastAPI` `lifespan` background `asyncio` task (confirmed via `inspect.signature` that `httpx.ASGITransport` never drives the lifespan protocol, so no existing test accidentally starts it). Placed in `campaigns/scheduler.py`, not `growixa_api.jobs` as the sprint doc sketched, since it's campaign-specific business logic co-located with the rest of that domain, not generic job plumbing. **Worker dispatcher (`GRX-SCHED-003`)**: `make_dispatch_handler` reuses `handle_send_campaign` unmodified — confirmed by reading it that it's status-agnostic and already idempotent via a `CampaignVersion`-existence check, so it's safely shared between the immediate "Send now" path and scheduled dispatch. **Idempotency & retry (`GRX-SCHED-004`)**: Redis marks a job's `idempotency_key` done *after* success, not before attempting, since claim-before-attempt would incorrectly block a legitimate retry after a transient failure — the DB-level `CampaignVersion` check remains the authoritative guard either way. Retries use the RabbitMQ TTL+dead-letter-exchange delay pattern (three durable wait queues with `x-message-ttl` 60000/300000/900000ms and `x-dead-letter-routing-key` back to `grx.campaigns.dispatch` — no delay plugin needed) rather than a client-side sleep, so retries survive a worker restart. **DLQ (`GRX-SCHED-005`'s DLQ half — the cancel-endpoint half already shipped under `GRX-SCHED-001`)**: after `MAX_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS` (3) the job is republished to `grx.campaigns.dlq` and the campaign is marked `FAILED`. **Tests (`GRX-SCHED-006`)**: 3 ticker tests (claim-scoping, one-job-per-claim, no-op-when-nothing-due) against real Postgres; 4 dispatch-consumer tests (idempotency skip, mark-done-after-success, retry-queue routing, DLQ+FAILED-after-max-attempts) against real Postgres with a fake in-memory Redis/AMQP-channel stand-in, since what's under test is consumer.py's own routing decisions, not aio_pika's/redis-py's wire behavior. **Two real bugs found and fixed along the way, neither assumed**: (1) `caf1c42204c9`'s `downgrade()` and `4a92b8107c12`'s `downgrade()` both dropped a unique constraint of the same name (`uq_campaigns_idempotency_key`) — harmless on the way up (redundant no-op) but fatal on the way down (`test_alembic_upgrade_head_then_downgrade_base_round_trips_cleanly` failed with "constraint does not exist" on the second drop); root-caused by testing single-step vs. multi-step downgrades directly via `alembic.command`, not by guessing — fixed by making `caf1c42204c9`'s upgrade/downgrade both no-ops, since its only job was already fully subsumed by `4a92b8107c12`'s own (correct) definition; it stays in the revision chain purely as a historical marker. (2) The live `growixa-api-1`/Compose container had **zero volume mounts** (`docker inspect` showed `Mounts: []`) despite `compose.yaml` defining bind mounts for `src`/`migrations` — it had been created before those mounts existed in `compose.yaml` and `docker compose restart` doesn't reapply config (only recreation does), so it had been silently serving a stale baked-in image this entire session; `docker compose up -d --build api` recreated it correctly. Caught while investigating why the scheduler's own log line never appeared live — which led to a third, smaller fix: nothing in `growixa_api` ever called `logging.basicConfig`, so `logging.getLogger("growixa_api")` had no handler and every `logger.info`/`.exception` call in `scheduler.py` was silently going nowhere (uvicorn only configures its own `uvicorn.*` loggers); added a `logging.basicConfig` call to `create_app()`. Live-verified against Compose after both fixes: the scheduler's startup log line appears, RabbitMQ (`rabbitmqctl list_queues`) shows all 5 queues with the correct TTL/DLX arguments, and multiple ticks ran with zero errors. `ruff`/`ruff format`/`mypy` clean on every file this row touched, both apps; `alembic check` clean. Description: `ai/capabilities/*.py` (six capabilities, `run(input, provider)` shape) + `ai/prompts/templates.py` (reads `brand_profiles.brand_voice`) + `POST /ai/generate/{capability}` gated `ai.manage`, writes `ai_generations` + `usage_records`

Required Tests: Live-verified against a real provider — see evidence; unit tests deferred to `GRX-AI-008`
Evidence: Each `capabilities/*.py` file is a thin wrapper (`run(input, provider, model) -> AIGenerationResult`) around its own `prompts/templates.py` builder function, per the plan's two constraints for future multi-agent reuse: the resolved provider is passed in (never re-resolved inside the capability), and prompt-string construction stays separate from the `provider.generate()` call. Prompt-injection posture (`THREAT_MODEL.md` T56): the system prompt is always fixed server-authored text plus the account's own `brand_profiles.brand_voice` (never per-request client input); customer-supplied `brief`/`existing_text` always lands in the user prompt, explicitly labeled as content to act on, never concatenated into the instruction position. `generate()` in `ai/services.py` resolves the effective provider first (raises `AINotConfiguredError`, no DB row written, before any vendor call); a provider-call failure after that point still writes a `FAILED` `ai_generations` row (provider/model are known by then) before raising `GenerationFailedError` — but a success writes `COMPLETE` plus a `usage_records` row (`operation_type='ai_generation'`), giving that table's zero-writers gap (Sprint 1, `DEC-GRX-007`) its first real data. Cost estimation (`_estimate_cost_usd`) uses a small hardcoded per-1K-token price table, explicitly approximate (not billing-grade), Ollama always $0. **Two real bugs found and fixed via live verification against a real provider** (the user set up their own Krutrim account — an OpenAI-compatible third-party API — as the platform default, `IITDEVELOPER` never saw the key): (1) `OpenAIProvider` originally hardcoded `api.openai.com`, so it couldn't reach any OpenAI-compatible third-party API at all — fixed by adding an optional `base_url` override (SSRF-validated the same as Azure/Ollama's, defaults to the official endpoint when unset), which is also a real product improvement beyond the immediate bug (many providers offer OpenAI-compatible endpoints). (2) The chosen model (`gpt-oss-120b`, a reasoning model) hit `max_tokens=60` mid-chain-of-thought, leaving `message.content` null with `finish_reason="length"` — silently returned as a "successful" empty generation until fixed; added an explicit empty-content-after-success check to all four provider adapters (raises `AIProviderError` instead of silently succeeding with blank text) and raised every capability's `MAX_TOKENS` budget (300–800, up from 60–500) to give reasoning models room to think and still answer. **A third bug found independently**: `ai_generations.estimated_cost_usd`'s unscaled `Numeric` column stored a Python float's exact binary representation (e.g. `0.000569999999999999977...`) instead of the intended 6-decimal value; fixed via a new migration adding `Numeric(10, 6)` (hand-written — `alembic --autogenerate` didn't detect the precision-only change as drift), verified reversible and `alembic check` clean both before and after a downgrade/upgrade round-trip. `ruff`/`ruff format`/`mypy` clean; `apps/api` pytest 244 passed, 8 skipped (unchanged — no new test file yet, deferred to `GRX-AI-008`). **Live-verified all six capabilities end-to-end against the real Krutrim API**: SUBJECT_LINE, BODY_COPY, SOCIAL_CAPTION, REWRITE, HASHTAGS, and POSTING_TIME each returned real, coherent generated text with real token counts and a clean estimated cost; confirmed the `AINotConfiguredError`→409 path (before any provider was configured) and the `AIProviderError`→502 path (a real 401 from Anthropic against a deliberately-fake key used during `GRX-AI-005` testing) both worked correctly and logged/skipped `usage_records` exactly as designed. This is the first Slice 6 task marked `DONE` on real (not mocked, not fake-credential) provider evidence, satisfying `DEC-GRX-011` in full — not merely code-complete-pending-credentials like `GRX-AI-003`/`004`/`005` above it.

Task: SPF alignment check before binding a sender identity to a connection
Description: Implements [`DEC-GRX-035`](DECISIONS.md) points 4, 5, 6 — the guardrail that makes multi-SMTP safe rather than a foot-gun. Before an identity is bound to a connection, resolve the identity's domain SPF record and check whether the connection's host is authorised to send for that domain. A failing check **warns and requires an explicit override**, recorded in the audit event; it never silently proceeds. Rationale: routing `hello@brandA.com` through a relay `brandA.com` does not authorise causes SPF failure and DMARC rejection, and the damage is invisible until deliverability collapses — the customer discovers it as "our email stopped arriving", weeks later. Also in scope: **remove any silent fallback** to "an active connection of that provider" when an identity's connection is inactive (ambiguous once several are active, and it hides the error), and confirm no automatic failover between relays exists. **No new dependency** — `dnspython>=2.6` is already present from `GRX-SAAS-016`, and `email_validation/checks.py` already does async DNS lookups worth reusing rather than duplicating. DKIM is deliberately excluded: the customer's relay signs the message and Growixa does not know their selector.
Acceptance Criteria: Binding an identity to a relay whose host is not covered by the domain's SPF record produces a clear warning and requires explicit override; the override is audited; an identity pointing at an inactive connection produces a surfaced error rather than a silent reroute; a domain with no SPF record is reported as unverifiable rather than as passing
Required Tests: Integration: SPF-covered host passes; uncovered host warns and requires override; missing SPF record reports unverifiable; override is audited; inactive-connection send fails loudly. Use synthetic domains/fixtures — no real customer hosts in tests

Task: Personalization renderer — shared, channel-agnostic, plus email wiring
Description: Implements [`DEC-GRX-036`](DECISIONS.md) (APPROVED). Builds the shared module both channels and both processes call: the API (test-send, preview) and the worker (real send) — the worker resolves data independently of the API's repositories, so a renderer living inside either would have to be duplicated. Two token scopes per the decision: **recipient scope** (`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`, plus that account's custom fields) resolving from the `contacts` row, and **account/sender scope** (`{{company_name}}` → `company_profile.name`, `{{website_url}}` → `company_profile.website`, `{{sender_name}}` → the sending identity's `from_name`). Note `{{company_name}}` is **not** a missing contact column — `contacts` has none — it is an account-scope token that was never wired. Non-negotiables from the decision: **no template engine** (Jinja2/Mako on user-supplied templates is an SSTI surface — bounded pattern matching only, no expressions or attribute traversal); **allowlist**, never all contact data, and specifically never `source`, which can carry acquisition provenance that must not render to the person it describes; a `default` filter (`{{first_name \| default:"there"}}`) as the only filter; HTML escaping on by default; and unknown tokens **blocking** the send rather than rendering literally or blank. Also adds the per-custom-field \"usable in personalization\" flag (one migration).
Acceptance Criteria: A campaign send resolves recipient and account tokens per recipient; a token with no value uses its `default` or blocks if none; unknown tokens fail with the offending token named; values are HTML-escaped; internal fields including `source` are unresolvable by design; fields flagged unusable do not resolve; identical output from the API test-send and the worker send path
Required Tests: Unit: tokeniser, allowlist enforcement, default filter, escaping, unknown-token rejection, internal-field refusal. Integration: real campaign send renders per recipient; API and worker produce identical output for the same input; account isolation on custom-field resolution
Evidence: Merged via `6b4d920` (branch `feature/BACKEND/GRX-CONTENT-001`, reviewed commit `d987545`), independently reviewed and approved — `pr_reviews/feature-BACKEND-GRX-CONTENT-001.md`. Row was left at `IN_PROGRESS` after merge; corrected here.

Task: Personalization frontend — real token picker + pre-send preview
Description: Upgrades the template editor's existing static 3-token toolbar (`first_name`/`last_name`/`company_name`, which `GRX-CONTENT-001` already made functional) to one driven by the **actual** tokens available for that account and channel, not a hardcoded list of three: standard recipient fields, that account's personalization-enabled custom fields, and the account/sender tokens. Implements `DEC-GRX-036` point 8 — a pre-send preview rendering against a real recipient, **plus a per-token count of how many recipients are missing a value**. That second half is the point: for bulk personalized sending it is the only thing that turns "looks right for the one I checked" into "safe for all 300". Discovering that 40 of 300 rendered blank after sending is the expensive way to learn. Must also surface which tokens are unavailable on broadcast channels (`DEC-GRX-036`'s scope table) rather than offering them and failing later.
Acceptance Criteria: Token picker lists only tokens that can actually resolve for this account and channel; preview renders against a chosen real recipient; missing-value counts shown per token before send; recipient-scope tokens are not offered on broadcast channels
Required Tests: Frontend component tests: picker contents driven by account data, preview rendering, missing-value reporting, broadcast-channel token filtering

Task: Account-scope tokens for social and future broadcast channels
Description: The "any campaign, not just email" half of `DEC-GRX-036`. `publish_social_post.py` has no substitution either (verified: zero matches). Broadcast channels have **no individual recipient**, so recipient-scope tokens cannot resolve there and must be **rejected at save time** rather than silently rendering blank at publish. Account/sender-scope tokens (`{{company_name}}`, `{{website_url}}`) do resolve and are what makes personalization meaningful beyond email. Same shared renderer as `GRX-CONTENT-001` — no second implementation. Deliberately sized small; the same wiring serves SMS (`GRX-FEAT-SMS-001`) and Telegram bot DM (`GRX-FEAT-034`) later, where recipient scope *does* apply because those are per-recipient channels.
Acceptance Criteria: Social post bodies resolve account/sender tokens at publish; a recipient-scope token in a broadcast post is rejected when saved, with a message explaining why; no duplicate renderer implementation
Required Tests: Integration: social publish renders account tokens; recipient-token rejection on save; shared-renderer reuse asserted
